summary: You take the core courses, STEMREM 802 once you reach TGR, a grant writing course and 10 units of electives (biochemistry, advanced genetics, genomics or cell biology, and science electives), each letter graded where offered with a B or better, toward 135 units of coursework and research. Rotations, the Stem Cell Club presentation, a submitted manuscript, the qualifying exam, the oral exam, committee meetings and the dissertation are checked by hand, as are the MSTP students' reduced course list and the 80 units due by the end of the second year.

node.name: Laboratory rotations in the first year and a thesis lab

add.why: "Each student should complete three one-quarter laboratory rotations during their first year, with two one-quarter laboratory rotations being the minimum in special circumstances ...
